cards.text: Friend, the workers have been building the tabernacle, with its curtains, frames and furniture (Exodus 36-38). Now it's time for clothes. Out of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, they make specially woven garments, plus the holy garments for Aaron, the brother of Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 4:14).

cards.question: True or false: the workers design these holy garments however they think looks best.
The workers make these specially woven garments for ___ in the sanctuary.

cards.text: First up is the ephod, which Bezalel, the craftsman from the tribe of Judah (Exodus 31:2), makes from finely spun linen, blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and threads cut from thin sheets of hammered gold. GOLD thread, friend, and the fanciest thing I own is an apron with a dough stain on it.

cards.question: The ephod gets shoulder pieces attached at two of its corners. What are they for?

answers.text: So it can be fastened on
So it can be hung up at night
So it can be stretched on a frame

cards.text: The ephod's woven waistband is all one piece with it. Then onyx stones go into gold filigree settings, engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel, and get fastened onto the shoulder pieces.

cards.question: The onyx stones go on the ephod's shoulder pieces as ___ stones for the sons of Israel.

cards.text: Then comes the breastpiece, made with the same workmanship as the ephod. Four rows of gemstones go on it, three to a row, from a ruby, a topaz and an emerald down to a beryl, an onyx and a jasper. Friend, I can't even get sprinkles to sit in a straight line.

cards.question: True or false: each of the twelve stones on the breastpiece is engraved with the name of one of the twelve tribes.

cards.text: For the breastpiece, they make braided chains of pure gold and a set of gold rings. The chains run up to the ephod's shoulder pieces, and more rings go on the breastpiece's other corners and on the front of the ephod, just above the waistband.

cards.question: Last step: they tie the breastpiece's rings to the ephod's rings with a cord of blue yarn. Why?

answers.text: So it won't swing out from the ephod
So it can come off in a hurry
So the stones won't scratch the linen

cards.text: And there it is: "just as the LORD had commanded Moses." They follow the plan to the letter, and I respect it, because the one time I winged a batch, the smoke alarm gave me a STANDING OVATION.
Next up is the robe of the ephod, woven entirely of blue cloth. It has an opening in the center, with a collar around it.

cards.question: The robe has an opening in the center, with a collar around it. What's the collar for?

answers.text: So it sits higher on the neck
So it can be tied shut

cards.text: Around the lower hem go pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen, with bells of pure gold between them. All those bells remind me of Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids, who's shaped like a bell, and when she had something to say, the WHOLE kitchen heard it.
Then come the linen pieces: tunics, a turban, ornate headbands, undergarments and a sash embroidered with blue, purple and scarlet yarn.

cards.question: True or false: the linen tunics are made for Aaron alone.

cards.text: Then comes a plate of pure gold for the crown. They engrave it like an inscription on a seal.

cards.question: What words do they engrave on the crown's gold plate?
They fasten a blue cord to the gold plate to mount it on the ___.
True or false: once the holy crown is made, all the work for the tabernacle is complete.

cards.text: Then they bring it all to Moses: the tent and its frames, the ark and the mercy seat, the table with the Bread of the Presence, the lampstand, both altars, the courtyard curtains, right down to the tent pegs and the priests' garments. The Israelites have done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses. Friend, if somebody asked to see ALL my work at once, I'd be hiding behind the oven.

cards.question: Moses inspects all the work and sees they did it just as the LORD had commanded. So what does Moses do?

answers.text: He gives them a day off

cards.text: We'll pause right here, friend, because this story isn't over yet.
